results.market_title: Will the highest temperature in Busan be 32°C on August 30?
results.reasoning: AccuWeather's extended 45-day calendar forecast for Gimhae/Busan area shows a projected high near 88°F (≈31°C) on August 30, 2026, close to but not exactly matching the 32°C threshold. Climatological normals for late August at Gimhae are around 28-30°C, with day-to-day highs commonly ranging 29-33°C during warm spells, meaning 32°C is a plausible but not the most likely single value among several whole-degree outcomes. Given the forecast lead time (over a day out, from an extended/statistical model rather than a short-range forecast) carries meaningful uncertainty, and 31°C or 33°C are roughly as likely as 32°C.
results.key_findings: ["AccuWeather's monthly calendar view for Busan showed a forecast high of 88°F (≈31.1°C, rounds to 31°C) for August 30","Adjacent days (Aug 31) showed 87°F (≈30.6°C), suggesting a cooling trend near the date","Climatological average high for Busan/Gimhae in late August is roughly 83-86°F (28-30°C), somewhat below the specific forecast","No short-range (1-3 day) forecast data was available confirming Aug 30 conditions precisely due to date mismatch between real-time search results and the stated 2026 date"]

results.market_title: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the September 2026 meeting?
results.reasoning: The Fed is in an unusual mid-cycle debate between renewed hawkish inflation/energy pressure and a weakening labor market. Live prediction markets (Kalshi, ~$16M volume) as of late August 2026 price a 25bp September hike at roughly 30-31%, implying ~69-70% for 'no change,' and weak July/August jobs data (per Motley Fool, Aug 12) has caused hike odds to 'plunge' from earlier July highs near 50%+. Wall Street desks are split (Goldman calling a hike 'very unlikely,' JPMorgan flagging a hike as newly plausible amid energy shocks), but the most recent, highest-liquidity market signal leans toward a hold rather than a hike.
results.key_findings: ["Kalshi's live Sept 2026 FOMC market prices Hike 25bps at ~31% (No 70%) as of late August 2026","DeFiRate aggregation of Kalshi/Polymarket shows 67.9% probability of holding steady, 30.5% for a 25bp hike after Aug 19 FOMC minutes","Motley Fool (Aug 12, 2026): 'odds of a September rate hike have plunged' after a weak jobs report, despite hawkish tilt at July meeting (3 dissents favoring a hike)","MUFG Research (Aug 2026) expects Fed to stay on hold through 2026, seeing 30-60% hike probability priced per meeting but doubting urgency to hike","Current target range is 3.50%-3.75% under new Chair Kevin Warsh, unchanged for five consecutive meetings through July 2026"]

results.market_title: Will MrBeast hit 139 billion views by August 31?
results.reasoning: Cross-referencing multiple third-party trackers (vidIQ, ChannelMetrics, VidMaestro, HypeAuditor subscriber counts) and extrapolating from a known June 27 (131.3B) to Aug 9 (136.35B) growth rate of ~117M views/day, MrBeast's channel is estimated to sit at roughly 138.6-138.8B total views as of Aug 29, 2026, needing about 300-400M more views in the ~2.5 days remaining until the Aug 31 11:59pm ET deadline — almost exactly matching his typical daily growth rate, making this a near coin-flip. A newly implemented YouTube policy (effective 8/24/2026) that counts views from the first frame rather than after ~30 seconds could modestly accelerate view accrual right in this window, providing some upside tilt, while data noise across trackers (ranging from 133.7B to 138.3B for supposedly 'current' figures) creates meaningful uncertainty in the true starting point.
results.key_findings: ["vidIQ shows MrBeast at 138,296,359,751 total views with 515M subscribers, gaining ~3.19B views in the trailing 28 days (~114M/day)","HypeAuditor confirms ~514.4M subscribers as the current August 2026 figure, corroborating vidIQ's recency","VidMaestro (updated Aug 9, 2026) showed 136.35B views/512M subs; extrapolating the implied ~117M views/day growth rate to Aug 29 lands at ~138.7B, just under the 139B threshold with ~2.5 days left","A YouTube-wide policy change effective 8/24/2026 counts views instantly from first-frame play (like TikTok/Instagram) rather than after ~30 seconds, which YouTube itself said would make 'total view counts move faster' — a tailwind for reaching the threshold in this exact window","A prior similar market ('hit 120B by April 30') resolved NO after landing at ~119.6B, showing these round-number thresholds have recently been narrowly missed"]

Will the Sweden Democrats (SD) win the third most seats in the 2026 Swedish parliamentary election?
results.reasoning: Multiple independent polling aggregators (PolitPro, Ipsos, Polara) consistently show Sverigedemokraterna (SD) polling around 19-20%, ahead of Moderaterna at roughly 17.5-18%, giving SD a fairly stable ~1.5-2.5 point lead and translating to seat projections of roughly SD 70 seats vs. M 65-69 seats. This gap has persisted across many polls and pollsters over recent months, making SD landing in second place (not third) the clear base case, mirroring the 2022 election outcome where SD also finished second ahead of M. For SD to fall to third, M would need to close and overtake a multi-point, multi-pollster gap in the final weeks — possible but not the current trend, so I estimate the probability of SD finishing third at around 15%, below the market's 33% crowd price.
